```{python}
#| label: setup
import hashlib
import json
import platform
import subprocess
import sys
import zipfile
from importlib.metadata import version
from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import yaml

sys.path.insert(0, "scripts/figures")
import style  # the paper's palette and fonts (scripts/figures/style.py)
from style import CTX, INK2, OURS, OURS_LIGHT, PLATE, VIEW, GRID, LINE, plt

%matplotlib inline

cfg = yaml.safe_load(Path("config/config.yaml").read_text())
demo = cfg["demo"]
res = Path(demo["results"])
scores = pd.read_csv(res / "scores.csv")
weights = pd.read_csv(res / "weights.csv")
summary = json.loads((res / "summary.json").read_text())
arms, data = summary["arms"], summary["data"]
truth = np.load(Path(demo["data_root"]) / "derived/xpert_sdst/v1/truth.npz")
var = {k: float(truth[k].var()) for k in ("context", "compound", "noise")}
share = {k: v / sum(var.values()) for k, v in var.items()}

ud, first, bb = arms["ctx_pc"], arms["pool_kta"], arms["mlp"]
plate, ceiling = arms["plate_baseline"], arms["noise_ceiling"]
f3 = lambda x: f"{x:.3f}"  # noqa: E731
pct = lambda x: f"{100 * x:.0f}%"  # noqa: E731
```

## Summary

UnDetect [@lei2027undetect] predicts the transcriptional response to a compound that was never profiled in any cell
line. A drug-free backbone network predicts, from the paired control profile, the response that any compound would
show in that sample; a multi-view kernel over chemical structure, targets, mechanism of action (MOA) and Cell Painting
morphology then transfers the residual responses of profiled compounds to unprofiled ones.

This report comes from the demo run of the pipeline (`pixi run reproduce`). The paper's own scripts ran unchanged, on
a simulated benchmark of the same shape as the paper's data, with real compounds and a known answer. On it, UnDetect
reached a PCC~DEG~ of `{python} f3(ud["deg_mean"])` (standard deviation `{python} f3(ud["deg_sd"])` over the five
compound-disjoint test folds), `{python} f3(ud["deg_mean"] - bb["deg_mean"])` above its own drug-free backbone
(`{python} f3(bb["deg_mean"])`). The ceiling set by the simulated noise is `{python} f3(ceiling["deg_mean"])`. These
numbers describe the simulation, not the paper's results.

## Why a demo

The paper's benchmark, the XPert L1000 drug-blind release [@guo2025xpert] used by @bai2026archive, has 78,453
control and treated L1000 profiles [@subramanian2017] of 8,276 compounds in 164 cell lines. It is a 1.6 GB download,
and the paper's runs take hours on a Slurm cluster. The demo keeps the shape of the problem and makes it small:

```{python}
#| label: tbl-shape
#| tbl-cap: "The paper's benchmark and the simulated benchmark of the demo. Both use 978 landmark genes and five folds that hold out whole compounds."
shape = pd.DataFrame(
    {"Paper (XPert L1000 drug-blind)": ["78,453", "8,276", "164", "978", "5"],
     "Demo (simulated)": [f"{data['n']:,}", f"{data['drugs']:,}", f"{data['cells']}", f"{data['genes']}", "5"]},
    index=["Samples (control, treated pairs)", "Compounds", "Cell lines", "Genes", "Compound-disjoint folds"])
shape
```

What is real and what is simulated:

- **Real:** the `{python} data["drugs"]` compounds, `{python} demo["simulation"]["compounds_per_class"]` from
  each of the `{python} data["moa_classes"]` most common MOA classes of the CLUE LINCS2020 compound table
  [@clue2020], with their structures, targets and MOA; the published models' scores in the next section.
- **Simulated** (seed `{python} demo["seed"]`, settings in `config/config.yaml`): the Cell Painting profiles of
  `{python} data["with_cell_painting"]` compounds, the control profiles of `{python} data["plates"]` assay plates in
  `{python} data["cells"]` cell lines, and every response. A response is a context term (a fixed nonlinear function
  of the control profile) plus a plate effect, plus a compound effect, plus noise. The compound effect is drawn
  from a Gaussian process whose covariance combines the four compound kernels with known weights, so compounds that
  are similar in a view respond alike. Of the response variance, the context and plate account for
  `{python} pct(share["context"])`, the compound effect for `{python} pct(share["compound"])` and noise for
  `{python} pct(share["noise"])`.

The split follows the benchmark's rule (`scripts/prep_xpert_sdst.py`): every compound is in the test set of exactly
one fold, every cell line is seen in training.

## The real benchmark: published models barely use the compound

The published models' scores on the real benchmark come from the archive of @bai2026archive, downloaded and checked
against its checksum by the pipeline. Setting a model's drug input to zero changes its PCC~DEG~ very little
(@tbl-published), which is the observation UnDetect starts from.

```{python}
#| label: tbl-published
#| tbl-cap: "PCC~DEG~ of the seven published models on the real drug-blind benchmark, with their drug input (Full) and with it set to zero (Zero): mean and standard deviation over the five folds, from `statistics/primary_comparisons.csv` of @bai2026archive."
with zipfile.ZipFile(cfg["published_metrics"]) as zf:
    pc = pd.read_csv(zf.open("benchmark_metrics/statistics/primary_comparisons.csv"))
z = pc[(pc.metric_key == "pcc_deg_mean") & (pc.contrast == "Full - Zero")].set_index("model")
full = z[[f"fold_{i}_full" for i in range(5)]].to_numpy()
zero = z[[f"fold_{i}_comparator" for i in range(5)]].to_numpy()
pub = pd.DataFrame({"Full": full.mean(1), "SD (Full)": full.std(1, ddof=1),
                    "Zero": zero.mean(1), "SD (Zero)": zero.std(1, ddof=1),
                    "Full − Zero": (full - zero).mean(1)}, index=z.index.rename("Model"))
pub = pub.sort_values("Full", ascending=False)
biggest = pub["Full − Zero"].idxmax()
pub.round(3)
```

The largest gain from the drug input is `{python} f3(pub.loc[biggest, "Full − Zero"])` (`{python} biggest`);
`{python} int((pub["Full − Zero"] < 0).sum())` of the `{python} len(pub)` models score higher without it.

## Results on the simulated benchmark

```{python}
#| label: tbl-scores
#| tbl-cap: "Scores on the simulated benchmark, mean ± standard deviation over the five test folds. PCC~DEG~: Pearson correlation of true and predicted response across genes, averaged over test samples. PCC~plate~: the same after subtracting the mean training response of the sample's plate, on samples whose plate has training samples."
order = ["cell_line_mean", "plate_baseline", "mlp", "pool_kta", "ctx_pc", "noise_ceiling"]
tab = pd.DataFrame(
    {"PCC_DEG": [f"{arms[a]['deg_mean']:.3f} ± {arms[a]['deg_sd']:.3f}" for a in order],
     "PCC_plate": [f"{arms[a]['plate_mean']:.3f} ± {arms[a]['plate_sd']:.3f}" for a in order]},
    index=pd.Index([arms[a]["label"] for a in order], name="Method"))
tab
```

The drug-free backbone learns the context from the control profile alone and reaches a PCC~DEG~ of
`{python} f3(bb["deg_mean"])`, against `{python} f3(plate["deg_mean"])` for the plate response baseline, which
predicts the mean training response of the sample's plate. The compound term of UnDetect's first stage raises this to
`{python} f3(first["deg_mean"])`, and the context-gated second stage to `{python} f3(ud["deg_mean"])`
(@tbl-scores, @fig-scores). The plate-centred score PCC~plate~ removes what plate-mates share: there the backbone
scores `{python} f3(bb["plate_mean"])` and UnDetect `{python} f3(ud["plate_mean"])`, so the gain comes from the
compounds, not from the plates.

```{python}
#| label: fig-scores
#| fig-cap: "PCC~DEG~ (left) and PCC~plate~ (right) on the simulated benchmark. Bars: mean over the five compound-disjoint test folds; error bars: standard deviation over folds; dots: single folds."
#| fig-alt: "Two horizontal bar charts with one bar per method: cell-line mean, plate response baseline, drug-free backbone, UnDetect first stage, UnDetect and the noise ceiling. The left chart shows PCC_DEG, the right chart PCC_plate, each with error bars and one dot per fold."
colour = {"cell_line_mean": LINE, "plate_baseline": PLATE, "mlp": CTX, "pool_kta": OURS_LIGHT, "ctx_pc": OURS,
          "noise_ceiling": "#ffffff"}
fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(7.5, 3.0), sharey=True)
for ax, metric, title in zip(axes, ("deg", "plate"), ("PCC$_\\mathrm{DEG}$", "PCC$_\\mathrm{plate}$")):
    for y, a in enumerate(order):
        v = scores.loc[scores.arm == a, metric].to_numpy()
        ax.barh(y, v.mean(), xerr=v.std(ddof=1), color=colour[a], edgecolor=INK2 if a == "noise_ceiling" else colour[a],
                linewidth=0.6, height=0.62, error_kw=dict(ecolor=INK2, elinewidth=0.7, capsize=2), zorder=2)
        ax.scatter(v, np.full(len(v), y) + np.linspace(-0.15, 0.15, len(v)), s=6, color=INK2, zorder=3)
    ax.set_yticks(range(len(order)), [arms[a]["label"] for a in order])
    ax.set_xlabel(title)
    ax.grid(axis="x", color=GRID, lw=0.6)
    ax.set_axisbelow(True)
    ax.set_xlim(left=0)
axes[0].invert_yaxis()
fig.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

UnDetect weights the four compound views by how well each view's kernel aligns with the training compounds' residual
responses (kernel-target alignment). @fig-weights sets these learned weights next to the weights used to simulate the
compound effects.

```{python}
#| label: fig-weights
#| fig-cap: "Weight of each compound view: the weight used in the simulation and the weight UnDetect learned on the training compounds of each fold (mean, error bar: standard deviation over the five folds)."
#| fig-alt: "Grouped bar chart for four compound views: structure, targets, mechanism of action and Cell Painting. For each view, one bar shows the simulated weight and one the weight UnDetect learned, with error bars."
names = {"chem": "Structure", "tgt": "Targets", "moa": "MOA", "morph": "Cell Painting"}
vw = summary["view_weights"]
x = np.arange(len(vw))
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(5.0, 2.8))
ax.bar(x - 0.2, [vw[v]["simulated"] for v in vw], width=0.38, color="#ffffff",
       edgecolor=[VIEW[v] for v in vw], hatch="////", linewidth=0.8, label="simulated", zorder=2)
ax.bar(x + 0.2, [vw[v]["learned_mean"] for v in vw], yerr=[vw[v]["learned_sd"] for v in vw], width=0.38,
       color=[VIEW[v] for v in vw], error_kw=dict(ecolor=INK2, elinewidth=0.7, capsize=2), label="learned", zorder=2)
ax.set_xticks(x, [names[v] for v in vw])
ax.set_ylabel("View weight")
ax.grid(axis="y", color=GRID, lw=0.6)
ax.set_axisbelow(True)
from matplotlib.patches import Patch
ax.legend(handles=[Patch(facecolor="#ffffff", edgecolor=INK2, hatch="////", label="simulated"),
                   Patch(facecolor=INK2, label="learned by UnDetect")], frameon=False, fontsize=8)
fig.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

Alignment measures how well each view's kernel on its own matches the residual responses; it is not an estimate of
the weights in the simulation, so the two need not agree. Here the largest learned weight goes to
`{python} names[max(vw, key=lambda v: vw[v]["learned_mean"])]` and the largest simulated weight to
`{python} names[max(vw, key=lambda v: vw[v]["simulated"])]`.

## Software

All software comes from the Pixi environment `default`, installed from `pixi.lock`, which records the exact build of
every package for Linux and macOS. The report was rendered with:

```{python}
#| label: tbl-software
#| tbl-cap: "Versions of the main software, read when the report was rendered."
import matplotlib, rdkit, scipy, sklearn, torch  # noqa: E401
quarto = subprocess.run(["quarto", "--version"], capture_output=True, text=True).stdout.strip()
lock = hashlib.sha256(Path("pixi.lock").read_bytes()).hexdigest()
software = pd.DataFrame(
    {"Version": [platform.python_version(), np.__version__, scipy.__version__, pd.__version__, sklearn.__version__,
                 torch.__version__, rdkit.__version__, matplotlib.__version__, version("snakemake"), quarto]},
    index=pd.Index(["Python", "NumPy", "SciPy", "pandas", "scikit-learn", "PyTorch", "RDKit", "Matplotlib",
                    "Snakemake", "Quarto"], name="Software"))
software
```

Platform: `{python} platform.platform()`; `pixi.lock` SHA-256 `{python} lock[:12]`. PyTorch ran on the CPU with `{python} demo["undetect"]["epochs"]` backbone
epochs at most (the paper: 500, with early stopping on the validation compounds).

## Data availability

The CLUE compound table [@clue2020] and the benchmark archive of @bai2026archive are downloaded by
`scripts/download_data.py`, which checks them against the checksums in `metadata/checksums.sha256`;
`metadata/sources.tsv` lists every data source of the demo and of the full paper run, with licenses. The simulated
data are made by `scripts/demo/simulate_benchmark.py` and can be regenerated at any time. The paper's data are
public; the full run is described in the repository's `README.md`.
